title: Roleset pathways: SAML onboarding, audit-provenance mapping, and admin escalation design
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Produce an operational role model and mapping that ties RBAC v2 rolesets to SAML assertions, ensures immutable audit provenance for admin actions, and defines safe escalation and migration paths.
background: We are designing RBAC v2 to support hierarchical resource tenancy, fine-grained scopes, and predictable admin guardrails. This ticket focuses on the glue between identity provider assertions (SAML/IdP attributes), the roleset model used by runtime and console, and audit events required for compliance. Current gaps: (1) SAML attribute-to-role mapping is ad-hoc across services, (2) admin escalations lack clear provenance metadata in audit logs, (3) migration from RBAC v1 roles to v2 rolesets needs a reversible plan with minimal customer disruption.
acceptance_criteria: A mapping spec that consumes SAML attributes and emits roleset assignments in the backend (schema + examples)
Audit event schema that records: actor_id, actor_source (IdP|internal), assertion_id, roleset_before, roleset_after, justification_token, and immutable_event_id
API contract for roleset CRUD that validates SAML-derived claims vs. directory-sourced groups and returns a conflict resolution plan
Migration runbook with dry-run mode and rollback steps; demonstrated on staging with test tenant data
Security review completed and signed off by InfoSec; test coverage for mapping logic and audit integrity
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a lightweight policy layer 'roleset-pathway' that sits between SSO assertion ingestion and our role resolver. The pathway defines precedence (IdP-asserted > directory-group > manual binding), transformation hooks (regex mapping, claim normalization), and an audit binding which attaches an assertion_id and signed hash to any admin action resulting from that assertion. Rolesets remain declarative and tenant-scoped; pathways are tenant-configurable with a safe default profile.
data_model_notes: roleset: id (uuid), name, permissions: list(permission_id), scope: resource_path (e.g., /org/{org_id}/project/{project_id}), mutable: boolean
pathway: id, tenant_id, precedence_enum, claim_map: list(string mapping expressions), transform_script_ref
assertion_record (audit-only): assertion_id, idp_name, raw_claims_sha256, canonical_claims_json, ingested_at
audit_event additions: assertion_id (nullable), provenance_hash, escalation_chain: list(actor_id+timestamp)
saml_integration: Accept SAML attributes 'roles', 'groups', and custom 'x-redwood-roleset' claims where available
Pathway claim_map examples: 'urn:example:group' -> /^infra-admins$/ => roleset: 'infra.admin', 'urn:example:org' -> capture org_id for scoped roles
Validate assertion freshness and include assertion_id in audit payload; if assertion missing canonical claim, fall back to directory mapping
Support IdP-initiated provisioning events: cache a short-lived assertion_record and reconcile via async worker to avoid blocking login flows
audit_requirements: Every role binding/unbinding and admin escalation must emit an audit event with assertion_id when applicable
Audit events must be append-only, signed server-side (HMAC with rotation), and include the canonical roleset diff
Retention and export: events tagged for compliance exports; add queryable fields for assertion_id, actor_source, and justification_token
Alerting: generate high-severity alerts for cross-tenant escalations or when manual admin elevation occurs without a linked assertion_id
admin_controls_and_escalation: Define two escalation channels: 'delegated' (time-limited token based, recorded with justification_token) and 'breakglass' (requires 2FA + audit notification)
Delegated tokens are single-use JWTs signed by control-plane KMS, include roleset_id, expiry, and origin_assertion_id
Breakglass requires immediate tenant-owner notification and an immutable audit marker; automatic reversion option configurable per tenant
RBAC UI: surface assertion provenance on role bindings (hover/click) so admins can see how a role was granted
migration_plan: Phase 0: Export current RBAC v1 mappings and build a dry-run converter that produces roleset candidates but doesn't apply them
Phase 1: Allow tenants to opt-in to 'pathway simulation' where SAML inbound flows are annotated with proposed roleset assignments in the audit stream
Phase 2: Soft-apply rolesets for a subset of non-critical tenants; monitor rollback rate and permission regressions
Phase 3: Full apply with tenant opt-out window and rollback tooling (automatic revert for X hours)
api_contract_examples: POST /v2/tenants/{tid}/rolesets/{rid}/bindings -> body {subject:{type: 'assertion'|'user'|'group', id: 'assertion_id'|'user_id'}, justification_token?} returns binding_event_id
GET /v2/audit?assertion_id={id}&actor_id={id} -> returns list of audit events with provenance_hash
open_questions: How do we handle attribute-free SAML flows where IdP provides only a subject? (proposal: require directory sync as fallback)
Do we allow tenant-defined transform scripts (security risk) or only curated transforms maintained by Redwood?
What is the canonical authority for group membership when directory and assertion disagree? (proposal: configurable precedence with warnings)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Malicious IdP could assert elevated groups. Mitigation: require signed metadata and optional IdP onboarding verification; default to least-privilege for unknown IdPs
Risk: Audit tampering. Mitigation: sign events server-side with KMS and store event hashes in an append-only ledger service
Risk: Migration causing permission gaps. Mitigation: simulation mode + automatic rollback + staged rollout
